lead: six minutes in, and the man was legible to you. what you do with a reading that complete is enter something with the person on the spot, out loud, and it has been in force for nineteen years.
sun: what you offer a near-stranger is the same instrument you would offer anyone: entered out loud, both parties present, no probation in it. people who meet you get told the terms on the first evening and find them unchanged at the twentieth year, which is why a four-minute acquaintance can turn into a party to something before either of you has eaten. nothing in you treats an early agreement as a provisional one.
moon: The Glance does the choosing, at a distance, and does not release what it takes. the man you keep terms with was assembled out of a hesitation and the order he put two facts in. the same equipment reports, years ahead of anybody else, that the thing has finished. both readings land at identical certainty, and one of them has nowhere to go.
pull: you read him in six minutes, undertook him by the end of the evening, and have known for eleven years that it finished — and the arrangement has never been affected by the third fact.
tension: people who met you once and left with terms have no idea that a complete assessment of them was taken at the door, or that it has been revised downward twice without a single term moving. what comes round about you is that you are a good judge of character, which is true and lands wrong: the reading and the keeping are separate faculties, and only one of them can be switched off.
cost: strangers become permanent fixtures of your life inside one evening, and they hold for thirty years, and the judgement that put them there was sound on the night. what you cannot do is act on the later reading. the ending shows up in you at a resolution nobody would credit, and connects to no procedure, so it sits there being accurate for the rest of the arrangement.

lead: your word sits inside this place in about nine locations, and no document anywhere records any of it as a word. it runs as policy, and nobody has ever gone looking for the evening it was given.
sun: every load-bearing arrangement here began with one person saying something to another, level, nothing above either of them enforcing it. that is the only part of the operation you built. and because it was said in a room with a name over the door, it has been absorbed — the staff run it as procedure, your successor will inherit it as procedure, and two people know it was a promise.
moon: you arrived at a chair that predates you by three generations, and whether you are owed it is a question with no floor. the one part that is unambiguously yours is the promises — given at an even temperature, no visible strain, the way the chair requires. which is exactly why nobody has ever offered to release you from one. what looked costless does not attract mercy.
pull: nine people believe the institution is holding them. the institution holds nothing. you said something at a table once, level, to each of them, and you have not left the table.
tension: nobody can thank you for it, because the credit lands on a chair that was here before you, and nobody can renegotiate it either, since a policy cannot be taken apart at the table where it was made. the people who benefit assume there is a rule protecting them. you are the rule. you were twenty-nine when you became it, and the generosity that made it looks from outside like the building being well run.
cost: an outfit this size rarely holds a person's future safely, and here it does, because every undertaking inside it was made by somebody and kept by the same somebody for thirty years. leaving is the part with nothing in it. the promises cannot be resigned with the post and cannot be carried out of the building, so the retirement everyone plans for you is a date you have stopped picturing.

lead: the largest object in any room you walk into is something you agreed to at twenty-four, in a kitchen, about somebody else's child. The Mane fixes what it reads as from thirty paces, and you had no vote.
sun: the thing you did was ordinary and private: two people, a table, something said out loud and done for twenty years without anybody checking. what it became is an exhibit. people who have met you twice can recite it. it is accurate — no part of the display is inflated, nothing has been staged — which is why it is impossible to correct. the reputation is true at exactly the size that embarrasses you.
moon: there is no small version of this. what registers across a room is set by the spread rather than by what you meant it to say, so the promise is at full width before you speak. people arrive already knowing the terms and assuming there is more where that came from, because a thing that size reads as surplus. nothing is in reserve. there is no reserve.
pull: you made one quiet promise and it has been the loudest thing about you for twenty years, and there is no volume control on it, and every word of it is true.
tension: solid arrives in a room ahead of you, and it recruits. people you barely know propose things on the strength of it, and you enter them, because entering is what you do and the reputation has promised them you will. nor could the two of you agree to stop — an audience that signed nothing is holding the terms, and a release would have to be performed to a room that was never party to it.
cost: somebody can plan a decade around a sentence you said in passing, and be right to. that is rare, and it is visible from across a town. what nobody asks — because a thing that size looks self-evidently well — is what the arrangement is like from inside it, and no opening has ever come up in which to say. the display answers the question before anybody puts it.

lead: you can name the evening the feeling went — a wednesday, nothing said, no argument in it — and the arrangement it produced has run for twenty-two years since, exactly as written.
sun: the undertaking was made without reference to how you felt, which is why the weather going changed no term. the meals still happen. the bad fortnight in her family still gets covered by you. nobody in that house has had to wonder, and wondering is the thing that would have shown. an agreement made on purpose needs no topping up, and this one has had none since the evening it stopped being wanted.
moon: a thing that ends in you ends completely. there was no fading and there is no ember — the season shut, and what was inside it went out with it, entire. nothing here runs on a low flame. the flame went out on a date you could give, and the structure over it stands at full size, unchanged, unresentful, having never drawn on it.
pull: the love ended in one season, completely, on a date you could give. the marriage did not notice, and has not been a lesser marriage for one week of the twenty-two.
tension: every version of the account you would have to give sounds like an admission. told plainly it lands as cruelty; softened it lands as a lie. the two who could discuss it are the two inside it, and one is being kept beautifully and has no reason to raise anything. the faculty that ends things in you, which has removed a house, a trade and everyone from a decade in single seasons, has never been pointed at this.
cost: she has had a full spouse for twenty-two years, every week of it, and none of the slow souring that half-presence produces, because terms do not thin the way feeling thins. what it leaves is one closed room in the life, with no door and no witness in it, and the only person who could be told is the one person it would injure.
